term: Linguistics Research Center at UT Austin
definition: The Linguistics Research Center (LRC) at the University of Texas is a center for computational linguistics research & development.
details: It was directed by Prof. Winfred Lehmann until his death in 2007, and subsequently by Dr. Jonathan Slocum. Since its founding, virtually all projects at the LRC have involved processing natural language texts with the aid of computers. The principal activities of the Center at present focus on Indo-European languages and comprise historical study, lexicography, and web-based teaching; staff members engage in several independent but often complementary projects in these fields using a variety of software, almost all of it developed in-house.

explainer.lead: The Linguistics Research Center at the University of Texas is a center for computational linguistics research and development. It matters as a long-running site of computer-aided work on natural language texts, especially Indo-European languages.

tiers.eli5: It is a university lab where researchers use computers to study old and modern languages, building dictionaries and teaching materials.

The limitation is scope: activity is focused on these areas and languages rather than general-purpose NLP.
